about.title: Sonoma Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Sonoma draws a steady stream of visitors to its wineries, plaza shops, and historic downtown near Broadway and W Napa Street, and with that foot traffic comes a real risk of falls on poorly maintained walkways, tasting room floors, uneven parking lots, and staircases in older buildings. When a property owner or business fails to fix a known hazard or warn guests about it, California law may hold them accountable for the injuries that follow. These cases often hinge on what the owner knew, or should have known, before you got hurt. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your claim directly. Instead, we connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in our network who can review what happened, help you understand your options, and work on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. If a fall in Sonoma left you injured, reaching out costs you nothing and may help you protect your claim before evidence disappears.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Sonoma Fall

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather evidence, like maintenance logs or prior complaints, to establish that notice.

items.title: Video Evidence Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Sonoma businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can make a real difference in proving how the fall happened.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Still Allow Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you were partly responsible for the fall, though your share of fault may reduce the final amount.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Sonoma?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of injury to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a city building or public park, that deadline is much shorter and requires a separate claims process first. Talking to an attorney early helps make sure you don't miss a critical filing window.

items.question: What if I fell at a winery or tasting room in Sonoma?
items.answer: Wineries and tasting rooms are private businesses just like any store or restaurant, so the same premises liability rules apply. The key question is still whether the owner knew or should have known about the spilled wine, uneven flooring, or other hazard and failed to address it. An independent attorney can help evaluate the specific conditions and evidence in your situation.

items.question: Do I need proof the business knew about the hazard?
items.answer: Yes, California law generally requires showing the owner had notice of the dangerous condition, either because they created it, knew about it, or should have discovered it through reasonable inspection. This is often the most contested part of a slip and fall case. Photos, witness statements, and surveillance footage can all help build that picture.
